article_title: Evaluation of a Virtual Laboratory Platform in General Education on Quantum Information Science
citation: Hongbin Song. (2025). Evaluation of a Virtual Laboratory Platform in General Education on Quantum Information Science. General Education Division, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
title: QLab virtual laboratory platform with a Bell test experiment for undergraduate quantum entanglement learning
description: QLab is a commercially available virtual laboratory platform from Anhui Qasky Quantum Technology Co. Ltd. that "simulates a 3-D physical laboratory environment equipped with various optical devices and instruments", letting undergraduates without experimental expertise conduct a Bell test. The virtual experimental setup consists of three units: generation of a quantum entangled state, distribution of entangled photons, and measurement of quantum correlations. A guidebook outlining principles and operational procedures was distributed in advance, and platform fidelity was ensured through repeated testing.
requirements: A guidebook outlining the principles and operational procedures of the virtual experiment distributed to students in advance
Detailed instructor explanation of each optical device's function in theory before starting the experiment
constraints: Conducting such complex quantum experiments in a real laboratory is impractical for undergraduates due to limitations in equipment and experimental skills, which the virtual platform addresses
target_learners: undergraduates from diverse academic backgrounds, both science and arts, in general education courses
target_learning_goals: understanding the counterintuitive concept of quantum entanglement and the Bell test
examples: Students conducted the Bell test individually in 2022–2023 and 2023–2024, then collaboratively in groups in 2024–2025 during a two-hour tutorial session
key_sources: Hongbin Song. (2025). Evaluation of a Virtual Laboratory Platform in General Education on Quantum Information Science. General Education Division, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

article_title: The Quantum Learning Pyramid (QLP): A Novel, Holistic, Industry-Ready Curriculum and Pedagogical Methodology for Quantum Computing Education
citation: Arun Govindankutty. (2026). The Quantum Learning Pyramid (QLP): A Novel, Holistic, Industry-Ready Curriculum and Pedagogical Methodology for Quantum Computing Education. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16289v1
title: QLP modular curriculum: six core modules with defined competencies and four specialization pathways
description: The curriculum is organized into six core modules — QPhenom, QDesign, QSoftware, QHardware, QSystems, and QSociety — each aligned with QLP tiers and defined by explicit learning competencies and credit values (Table II). The article notes modules "may be offered as stand-alone courses or combined into sequences" and supports four specialization pathways: Quantum Theory, Quantum Engineering, Quantum Software, and Quantum Applications. Stackable micro-credentials such as Quantum Programming Foundations support workforce alignment, and the curriculum is explicitly aligned with the ACM/IEEE CS2023 "AR-Quantum: Quantum Architectures" knowledge unit.
requirements: Alignment of modules with explicit learning competencies and ACM/IEEE CS2023 guidelines
constraints: Institutions tailor programs to local constraints while preserving curricular coherence
target_learners: Introductory undergraduates through advanced graduate students
examples: A capstone implementation of Shor's algorithm on a simulator integrates introductory concepts; graduate offerings follow a two-course sequence
key_sources: Arun Govindankutty. (2026). The Quantum Learning Pyramid (QLP): A Novel, Holistic, Industry-Ready Curriculum and Pedagogical Methodology for Quantum Computing Education. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16289

article_title: The Quantum Learning Pyramid (QLP): A Novel, Holistic, Industry-Ready Curriculum and Pedagogical Methodology for Quantum Computing Education
citation: Arun Govindankutty. (2026). The Quantum Learning Pyramid (QLP): A Novel, Holistic, Industry-Ready Curriculum and Pedagogical Methodology for Quantum Computing Education. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16289v1
title: Multidimensional assessment matrix using validated quantum concept inventories (QCCS, QISCIT)
description: The QLP assessment framework integrates formative, summative, and authentic evaluations across conceptual, computational, experimental, and sociotechnical domains (Table III). Rather than introducing a new instrument, it leverages existing validated inventories: the Quantum Computing Conceptual Survey (QCCS) for introductory courses and the Quantum Information Science Concept Inventory Test (QISCIT) for learners without extensive mathematical prerequisites. A weighted composite score S = Σ wi Ci may be used when combining subscales, providing "a simple mechanism for diagnosing misconceptions and monitoring conceptual development".
requirements: Use of established, peer-reviewed assessment instruments
Shared assessment rubrics for interdisciplinary teaching
constraints: The article expects, but does not yet report, that thematic analysis of reflections will indicate increased engagement; no implementation data exist
target_learners: Undergraduate and graduate quantum computing students
target_learning_goals: Measuring conceptual understanding of superposition, entanglement, measurement, and the quantum-classical interface
examples: Formative conceptual assessment uses concept maps and peer instruction; authentic sociotechnical assessment asks students to develop responsible use guidelines
key_sources: Arun Govindankutty. (2026). The Quantum Learning Pyramid (QLP): A Novel, Holistic, Industry-Ready Curriculum and Pedagogical Methodology for Quantum Computing Education. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16289
